PROPOSED MEMORIAL TEMPLE ASSESSMENTS
There has been ref erred to the Committee on Policy and General
Purposes three resolutions proposing assessments for the construction
of the Memorial Temple.
One resolution proposes an assessment of $4.00 per year for a period
of four years against each member of the jurisdiction; to be paid annually at the time the member pays his Lodge dues and for which he is
to be billed by the Lodge Secretary-that any member who has heretofore contributed to the fund, shall, at his option, be given credit upon
said assessment in the amount of his voluntary contribution-that each
Lodge shall have authority to pay from its general funds on behalf of
any member unable to do so, any part of the assessment-that each
Lodge shall be liable for the full amount of the assessment, proportionate
to the membership of such Lodge, in the same manner it is liable for per
capita taxes levied by Grand Lodge.
The second resolution proposes that:
"The Grand Lodge of California reaffirms the goal recommended in
the 1953 Annual Communication with the understanding that if said
goal is not attained through voluntary subscription from the members,
that the difference between the voluntary subscription and the goal of
$10.00 per member shall be paid out of the general funds of the Lodge.
One half of said difference to be remitted not later than October 1, 1955,
and the balance not later than October 1, 1956-that the total of such
obligation shall be computed on the January 1. 1955 membership of the
Lodge.''
The third resolution proposes that, effective January l, 1955 and
ending December 31, 1958, an assessment of $16.00 shall be levied
against all present and/or future members within the life of the resolution, financially able to pay, to be paid either in one lump sum or in four
equal installments of four dollars each year, subject to the remission of,
and under the same conditions, as are dues, all funds when and as collected by the Secretary of subordinate Lodges to be remitted to the

286

287

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

Grand Lodge, together with and as a part of the annual report, or more
often if desired. The assessment to be collected from each applicant for
re-instatement and/or membership by affiliation from a Lodge in another
jurisdiction, when the member has not previously paid-that a Lodge
may pay the entire assessment against its membership from the general
funds of the Lodge, if it chooses so to do.
On the basis of the splendid record in so short a period of time, we
feel that the campaign should be continued on a voluntary basis as recommended by the Memorial Temple Committee, and that greater effort
be made by the Masters of the constituent Lodges to convince their
members that 'failure to achieve the goal on a voluntary basis will doubtless result in an assessment against the Lodges or the members individually at some later date.
We feel that at this time the resolutions to levy assessments should
not :be approved by this Grand Lodge.
Each .proposal for assessment was submitted to Grand Lodge separately.
Each proposal failed of adoption.

was empowered to proceed with the preparation of plans. The program
for a Temple was de8nitely under way!
At this Communication, we presented a report covering the results
of the directive given a year ago. The program of individual voluntary
contributions had produced a total slightly less than $900,000. These
contributions had been received from approximately 50,000 membersless than 25 % of our total membership. Only 40 odd Lodges were listed
on the Merit Roll (which named those Lodges having achieved the
quota of $10.00 per member).
The Memorial Temple Committee will determine the mechanical
plan which is to be followed during the coming year. They realize that
the setup of a year ago did not contemplate the lack of interest and the
lack of knowledge with reference to our Fraternity-which were true in
many instances. It is to be assumed that the program which they develop
for the coming year will include a method of overcoming this lack of
information and this lack of interest. It will be necessary to re-enthuse
the Past Masters of our Lodges. They must be brought to a realization
that their work was not finished when they accepted a title and secured
the right to wear the Past Master's Jewel. Every honor carries with it
responsibility. They have received the honor! They should now shoulder
the responsibility!
The average member must be brought to realize that he has a part
in the Grand Lodge. He takes pride in his Masonic membership. He is
aware that he could not be a member of the Fraternity without having
a Lodge in which to hold his membership. He must be reminded that the
Lodge would not pe possible were it not for the Grand Lodge. The Grand
Lodge issued the charter for his Lodge. The Grand Lodge is the central
organization in which his Lodge, together with the others, legislates for
the Fraternity in this Jurisdiction. Without the Grand Lodge, the individual member could not have the membership which he prizes. Both
groups must be brought to recall that portion of their obligation in
which they agreed to support the edicts and regulations of their Grand
Lodge. The financing and the building of a Temple are the decisions of
Grand Lodge. They have the force of an edict! The Past Masters and
the individual members are bound to respect and conform to that edict!
In concluding, Brother Siems reminded the representatives that the
decision as to procedure had been made by them, and that the responsibility for success rested with them.

REVIEW OF MEMORIAL TEMPLE PROGRAM
Past Grand Master Edward H. Siems, as Chairman of the Grand
Lodge Committee on Memorial Temple, pointed out to the brethren
that the Temple Committee accepted the decision of the representatives
to continue the program for raising funds on a voluntary basis. He emphasized that the Committee would formulate their plans in accordance
with the directive of the Annual Communication.
Brother Siems pointed out that a year of intensive activity had just
been completed following the planning of the project since 1947. Prior
to that date, there had been a realization that someday we must consider
a new home for Grand Lodge. Beginining in 1947 there had come an
acute realization that a decision must be reached now. Each year it has
become more evident that an adequate temple be provided-<>r an inescapable alternative be faced: without adequate meeting space each
Lodge in the jurisdiction would be limited to a single representative,
because the number attending on this basis would fill to capacity the
largest room available at 25 Van Ness Avenue. The Memorial Temple
Committee realizes that the adoption of this alternative would terminate
the democratic procedure of this Grand Lodge.
A year ago, the determination to build a Temple was reconsidered
and reiterated. The Memorial Temple Committee was given a directive
to proceed with the accumulation of funds. Their suggested program
(that each Lodge be requested to collect from its members an amount
equal to $10.00 per member) was approved. Emphasis was placed on the
propriety of individual contributions being equal to a day's pay. At this
time, the purchase of the site on ~ob Hill was ratified and the Committee

1953 annual returns.
Schedule 3: Comparison of budget and expenditures, 1953-54.
Exhibit C: Grand Treasurer's statement of cash receipts and disbursements, August 1, 1953 to July 31, 1954.
Exhibit D: Grand Secretary's resume of cash received, August 1, 1953 to
July 31, 1954.
Schedule 4: Statement of Masonic Homes per capita dues and $25.00
contributions collected during the year 1953-54.
Comments
As shown on Exhibit AA of this report, the combined assets of Grand
Lodge, the Masonic Homes and the Endowment Fund now exceed $11,500,000.00; an increase of $400,000.00 over last year. Exhibit BB shows that over
$3,000,000.00 was received and a like amount disbursed by these three entities.
Over one-half of the disbursements were for the purchase of securities and
other assets, for the transfer of cash among the funds, and to meet the obligations of the various funds. Grand Lodge maintains an adequate aystem of
safe-guards to insure the safety of this flow of money, and the safety of the
assets owned.
The above comments and figures do not include the cash and other
assets of the California Masonic Memorial Temple, a corporation organized
to own and operate the proposed Masonic Memorial Temple. We have prepared a separate report thereon.
The expenses and appropriations of Grand Lodge exceeded the revenue
received by $26,111.56. The main cause of this deficit was three unbudgeted
items which were approved by the Grand Master, earthquake damage allowance to Maricopa Building Association of $10,000.00 and Tehachapi Temple
Association of $5,000.00 and Memorial Temple Committee expenses of
$41,795.06.
Schedules 2 and 4 show proof of the revenue due from the Lodges in
accordance with their 1953 annual returns and the $25.00 Homes contributions reported received up to July 31, 1954. The total amount due, as shown,
agrees with the total cash received from the Lodges by the Grand Secretary.

InTestments $1.504.212.32
The bonds, stocks and investments included under this heading are
listed in detail on Schedule 1. This list include all securities of the Trust
and Special Purpose funds. However, the Trust Funds securities are carried
in separate portfolios and separate bank accounts are maintained in order
to a~ount for each trust fund in accordance with its agreement.
The investment account shows an increase of $138,318.06 over last year.
Bonds and stocks are listed at cost; donated securities are listed at market
value when received, if known, otherwise at nominal value of $1.00. Life
insurance policies are recorded at the amount due at the death of the insured if determinable and the premiums are fully paid up, otherwise at a
value of $1.00.
The notes and contracts receivable were received from the sales of
donated property and are listed at the unpaid balance at July 31, 1954. ·
Monthly payments of principal and interest have been received.
All bonds, stocks and notes are held by the Anglo California National
Bank and were verified by a certified list from the bank. The life insurance
policies and real estate deeds are held in the office of the Grand Secretary
and were inspected by us.

September 30, 1954
Maaonic Homes of California

Properties $2.988,918.12
The value of the properties as shown is the cost of the homes at Decoto
and Covina. During the current year $1,551.85 was paid for sound-proofing
the hospital and $1,458.48 for equipment at Decoto; and $3,480.92 for installation of a dumb-waiter and $6,940.95 for equipment at Covina. All of
these costs were expended from the Reserve for Additions and Replacements.
Funds Held in Trust $439,609.32
With the exception of the Residents' Deposits of $16,248.73, which are
personal money of the Decoto residents and the children at Covina, these
trust funds were created by donation or by bequest to the Homes for a
particular purpose. The activities of each fund during the current year are
shown on Schedule 2. Separate savings accounts are kept for each fund and
the securities are carried in separate portfolios.
The income due on the investments was received and deposited in the
proper .fund. ,Annuity payments were made as required by the contract
carried by the Wadleigh Endowment Fund. Payments from the other trust
funds were in accordance with the agreements. The Wadleigh Endowment
Fund is to be transferred to the Masonic Homes Endowment Fund after the
death of the annuitants.
Funds Held for Special Purposes Sl.020.512.61
These funds were created by the Board of Trustees to receive donations
and bequests which are to be used for purposes other than the direct operating expenses of the Homes. The activities of these funds during the current
year are shown on Schedule 3.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

315

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

Revenue and Expense
The 1953 annual returns from the Lodges were audited and the $25.00
contributions due thereon, plus the contributions received up to July 31, 1954,
agree with the amount turned over to the Grand Treasurer by the Grand
Secretary. The per capita on 210,819 members at 75c, in amount, $158,114.25,
was also received by the Grand Treasurer from the Grand Secretary. The
Endowment Fund income received by the Homes is in agreement with the
Endowment Fund audit report. All interest and dividends due on the investments were received. The records of the contributions through Lodges
were examined and the amounts appear to be all that can be collected.
The disbursements were made by checks and supported by proper
vouchers.
The operations of the Masonic Homes resulted in an excess of revenue
over expense amounting to $104,990.95 as shown by Exhibit B.
Accountant's Opinion
.
In my opinion, the accompanying balance sheet and statement of revenue
and expense present fairly the financial position of the Masonic Homes of
California at July 31, 1954 and the results of its operations for the fiscal
year ended July 31, 1954, in accordance with generally accepted accounting
principles applied on a basis consistent with that of the preceding years.
Respectfully submitted,
WALTER A. PARKER
Certified Public Accountant

ENDOWMENT FUND
GENTLEMEN:
We have audited the accounts and records of the MASONIC HOMES
ENDOWMENT FUND for the fiscal year ended July 31, 1954 and submit
·
herewith the following statements:
EXHIBIT A: STATEMENT OF ASSETS, JULY 31, 1954.
SCHEDULE 1: ENDOWMENT FUND SECURITIES OWNED,
JULY 31, 1954.
EXHIBIT B: STATEMENT OF CASH RECEIPTS AND DISBURSEMENTS, AUGUST 1, 1953 TO JULY 31, 1954.
SCHEDULE 2: SECURITIES REDEEMED AND SOLD DURING THE
FISCAL YEAR ENDED JULY 31, 1954.
EXHIBIT C: STATEMENT OF JOHN AND LENA LUCKENBACH
FUND, JULY 31, 1954.
EXHIBIT D: STATEMENT OF INCOME AND CAPITAL ACCOUNTS,
FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED JULY 31, 1954.
COMMENTS
Cash:
The bank balances were verified by correspondence with the depositaries. All interest and dividends due from investments and savings bank
accounts were received and deposited in the bank accounts of the Masonic
Homes of California. The total income received by the Homes from the
Endowment Fund amounted to $173,273.01 as compared to $155,052.86 for
last year.
Securities:
Securities owned on July 31, 1954 are listed on Schedule 1. Securities
redeemed and sold during the current year are listed on Schedule 2.
Stocks and bonds purchased are listed at cost. Donated securities are
listed at market value when received, or at a nominal value of $1.00 if the
actual value is unknown.
Certified lists of the securities held for the account of the Endowment
and Luckenbach Funds were received from the Anglo California National
Bank which has custody of the securities. The records were checked to these
lists and the securities not listed were inspected by us at the office of the
Grand Secretary.
Increase in Fund:
The combined assets of the Endowment Fund and the Luckenbach Fund
show the following increase for the current year:
Amount of funds, July 31, 195-L------ ----f 5,600,606.15
Amount of funds, July 31, 1953·-- · · - · · - - · - · -·- - 5,148,931.11

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

The donations received through Lodges were confirmed by correspondence with the individual Lodges as at June 15, 1954.
Other Endowment Assets:
The books of the Masonic Homes carry the record of the Harriet C. Wadleigh Endowment Annuity Fund. After the death of the beneficiaries of this
fund, the remainder will be transferred to the Endowment Fund. The
Masonic Homes audit report shows that this fund had a balance of $18,407.37
as at July 31, 1954.
The Masonic Homes also hold several pieces of real estate for the account
of the Endowment Fund. Whenever a sale is made the proceeds will be transferred to the account of the Endowment Fund.
Accountants' Opinion:

In our opinion, the accompanying statements present fairly the financial
position of the Masonic Homes Endowment Fund at July 31, 1954 in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles applied on a basis consistent with that of the preceding year.
Respectfully submitted,
WALTER A PARKER
Certified Public Accountant

CALIFORNIA MASONIC MEMORIAL TEMPLE AUDIT
CALIFORNIA MASONIC MEMORIAL TEMPLE
October 4, 1954
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA
GENTLEMEN:
We have examined the records of the CALIFORNIA MASONIC MEMORIAL TEMPLE, a corporation, from its beginning January 6 to July 31, 1954.
The building located on the property owned by the corporation is operated under the management of the James Hurst Company, a realty company.
We examined the records of the building operations as maintained by the
James Hurst Company and found them in order.
As a part of this report we attach hereto the' following statements:
EXHIBIT A: BALANCE SHEET, JULY 31, 1954.
EXHIBIT B: STATEMENT OF CASH RECEIPTS AND DISBURSEMENTS, JANUARY 6, 1954 TO JULY 31, 1954.
EXHIBIT C: STATEMENT OF REVENUE AND EXPENSE-PROPERTY OPERATIONS, SEPTEMBER 25, 1953 TO JULY 31, 1954.
COMMENTS
All receipts and expenditures have been included in the statements. All
amounts were verified with the exception of the contributions by individuals
in the amount of $504,607.18. The total contributions by individuals is the
amount deposited in the bank as coming from Masons throughout the State
of California. We were unable to verify this amount, or the amount of the
unpaid pledges by an examination of the pledge cards due to the fact that
the office procedure was in process of being changed over to a punch-card
system by the International Business Machine Corporation. As a result of
this change, a part of the pledge cards were at the I. B. M. office and were
not properly segregated nor readily available for a proper examination.
The cash balance as at July 31, 1954 was in the following banks:
Treasurer's bank accounts:
